text: {"summary":"Advisory review of the supplied delegation/operator-flow implementation. I found concrete concerns around (1) how delegation state gates a previously approved registration versus terminal revocation, (2) a possible operator view crash via non-null assertion on optional delegation, and (3) a weak query in the buyer delegation CAS that does not bind the delegation write to the seller/buyer relationship or quote payload. No tools were used; findings are based solely on the supplied source.","findings":[{"severity":"P1","file":"lib/integration-operator-store.ts","line":23,"title":"Operator view dereferences optional delegation without guarding","evidence":"view() unconditionally reads `delegationRevision:item.delegation!.revision`. Both decode() paths call assertAssignedIntegrationOperator which fails (404) when delegation is inactive/absent, so this is mostly protected for the operator queue. However listAssignedIntegrations SQL filters only on json_extract delegation.active=1/operatorId/buyerId equality and does not ensure the row's stored submitted_by / quote seller relation matches at query time; decode() re-checks, but view() is still the terminal sink. The non-null assertion is fragile if a row passes SQL filtering via type coercion (e.g. active stored as 1/true) while validateIntegrationDelegation later rejects boolean/type shapes, which would surface as a 503 rather than a clean exclusion.","reproduction":"Insert a seller_integration_requests row whose payload delegation.active is JSON true/1 and operatorId matches an actor, but whose delegation object otherwise fails validateIntegrationDelegation (e.g. events length mismatch). SQL `json_extract(... '$.delegation.active') = 1` matches; decode() throws a DomainError (503) instead of being excluded, so one malformed row can break the whole operator list response.","suggestion":"Filter more defensively at the SQL layer (e.g. require json_type(active)='true' and matching counts) or wrap per-row decode in a try/catch that skips inconsistent rows and logs, so single-row corruption cannot take down the entire assigned list. Remove the unsafe non-null assertion in view().","category":"robustness","session_id":"review-1","id":"F1"},{"severity":"P1","file":"lib/seller-integration-store.ts","line":39,"title":"Delegation CAS does not bind quote seller to the stored payload","evidence":"delegateIntegrationRequest's UPDATE guards `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM quotes q WHERE q.id=? AND q.owner_id=? AND q.version=?)` but does not re-check `q.seller_id` against `record.sellerId` nor that the stored delegation's buyerId still equals the quote owner. changeIntegrationDelegation validates existing.buyerId===buyerId against the request argument (record.buyerId), which derives from readProofCase. If readProofCase resolves buyer/seller from a quote snapshot that can drift from the DB row (as decideAssignedIntegration explicitly guards with owner_id and seller_id IS ?), the buyer delegation write can succeed against a row whose quote owner changed concurrently, since the CAS compares only version and owner_id, not seller_id.","reproduction":"Have buyer B delegate application A. Concurrently, quote.owner_id is reassigned or the proof-case seller changes; the version may or may not change. Because the delegation UPDATE only constrains owner_id=q.owner and version, a write based on a stale record.buyerId/sellerId read can still land if version matches, allowing a delegation decision formed under an old buyer/seller pairing.","suggestion":"Extend the delegation CAS to match `q.seller_id IS ?` (as decideAssignedIntegration does) and require stored payload delegation.buyerId equals q.owner_id, so both buyer and seller identity are pinned at write time.","category":"auth","session_id":"review-1","id":"F2"},{"severity":"P2","file":"lib/integration-delegation.ts","line":54,"title":"Approved target still gated by delegation state after terminal revocation","evidence":"integrationTargetEnabled returns approved && (!delegation||delegation.active). A terminal reject/revoke after approval (seller-integration store decision path allows approved->rejected) also flips integrationTargetEnabled false even though history keeps approved evidence. Conversely, if buyer withdraws review (delegation.active=false) on an already approved request, future testing admission is disabled while status stays 'approved'. Combined with seller resubmit logic (line 43 allows resubmit when actions are non-terminal OR delegation.active===false), a withdrawn (revoked) approved application can be resubmitted as a fresh 'requested' request without a new approval window tied to the same registration, and integrationTargetEnabled then sees delegation undefined -> admission re-enabled via the new request's path is not represented here, creating ambiguity about what actually authorizes testing.","reproduction":"New request -> grant -> approve (registration set). Buyer revoke-review. Status remains approved, registration retained, delegation.active=false so integrationTargetEnabled=false. Seller submits a resubmission (previousRequestId = withdrawn.id); newIntegrationRequest allows it because delegation.active===false. Client canSubmit gating (seller-integration-store line 16) does not consult integrationTargetEnabled, so a new pending request is created for the same delivery.","suggestion":"Explicitly define precedence: purchase/testing admission should be governed by current status plus a single canonical predicate, not OR-ed across delegation.active and a replacement request. On revoke of an approved request, consider marking status 'rejected' (or a dedicated 'revoked' status) so history and admission agree, and make resubmission require an explicit new approval rather than silently re-entering the requested queue.","category":"logic","session_id":"review-1","id":"F3"},{"severity":"P2","file":"lib/integration-delegation.ts","line":19,"title":"Delegation event buyerId for revoke is caller-supplied and not re-checked against prior buyer","evidence":"validateIntegrationDelegation checks `e.operatorId===e.buyerId`, operatorId!==sellerId, and buyerId continuity only for i>0 via `i>0&&e.buyerId!==buyerId`. It never checks the first grant event's buyerId against the request's actual buyer (submittedBy is the seller). IntegrationDelegation.buyerId is derived solely from event fields, so a crafted but internally-consistent delegation could carry a buyerId unrelated to the quote owner; it is only cross-checked later via assertAssignedIntegrationOperator against caller-supplied buyerId, not the persisted owner.","reproduction":"Construct a delegation where events[0].buyerId='attacker' and all internal checks (operatorId!==buyerId, continuity) hold; validateIntegrationDelegation passes because it has no seller/owner to compare against. Any code path relying on delegation.buyerId alone (e.g. json_extract buyerId = q.owner_id SQL filter) is the only barrier; if that filter is bypassed or quote owner equality differs, buyerId binding is not enforced inside the validator.","suggestion":"Pass the authoritative quote owner into validateIntegrationDelegation (or validate in store decode after fetching the quote owner) and assert each grant event's buyerId equals the actual buyer, matching the SQL filter so validator and query agree.","category":"auth","session_id":"review-1","id":"F4"}],"limitations":["No tools were available; conclusions are static and based on the supplied snippets only. Files imported by the reviewed code (domain.ts, proof-store, contracts.ts, runtime-project.ts, server.ts, and SQL schema) were not supplied, so authoritative behavior of readProofCase role/buyer/seller resolution, integrationDelivery, quote version semantics, and DB collation/JSON typing is inferred.","Whether the SQL json_extract '$.delegation.active' = 1 filter can match malformed or coercible rows depends on the DB engine and stored encoding, which was not supplied.","The exact interaction between registration admission consumers (approvedIntegrationRegistrations) and resubmitted pending requests was not supplied, so finding F3's downstream effect is bounded to supplied predicates.","Legacy owner+operator flow was not provided in source, so preservation of that path could not be verified."]}
